input.prompt: An authentic Srikalahasti kalamkari hand-painted cotton textile panel, a sibling of the reference image: match its exact palette, kalam line quality, dotted and cross-hatched fill patterns, visible cotton weave and its lotus-and-vine border, but with a NEW composition (do not copy the reference's central tree or its peacocks). Photographed flat and straight-on so the cloth fills the entire frame edge to edge. The ground of the panel is undyed ecru cotton. COMPOSITION, exactly two people: a young Telugu man and a young Telugu woman sit cross-legged on a patterned madder-red mat in the lower half, facing each other in side profile, both mid-conversation with one hand raised in an open, expressive talking gesture. The man (left) has short black hair, a neat short black beard and clearly visible black-rimmed round spectacles over his almond eye, and wears a kurta with a dotted indigo pattern. The woman (right) has long black hair in a single braid down her back, and wears a madder-red saree with a yellow border and fine dot pattern. Both drawn in the classical kalamkari manner: large almond eyes, gentle smiles, stylised hands with five slender fingers, flowing patterned drapery. THE KEY MOTIF: from just in front of each of their mouths, a slender curling green vine with small leaves springs out and rises, the man's vine and the woman's vine curving toward each other, twisting around each other twice in the open ecru space between and above their heads, and joining into ONE single large blooming pink-and-madder lotus flower that floats directly above and between their heads, the clear focal point of the panel. A single blossoming tree grows at the far left edge behind the man, its trunk at the side, its curling branches arching across the top of the panel like a canopy with lotus blossoms, paisley leaves and buds. On the one branch directly above the central lotus, exactly two green parrots perch side by side, close together, facing each other beak to beak, each with one foot raised, mirroring the couple below. Only two birds in the whole panel. A small band of stylised flowering ground beneath the mat. A dense ornamental border runs around all four edges: a lotus-and-vine scroll on madder red between two thin dotted bands, identical in style to the reference. Style: freehand kalam (bamboo pen) outlines in iron-black with confident, slightly irregular line weight; flat natural vegetable-dye fills only: deep madder red, brick red, indigo blue, myrobalan-turmeric yellow, green from indigo over yellow, and undyed ecru cotton; dense hand-drawn fills of dots, cross-hatching, scales and tiny petals; slight dye bleed at colour edges. Completely flat, no perspective, no shading, no gradients, no metallic gold, no 3D, no photorealism. The vines are purely botanical, with leaves and tendrils only. No text, no letters, no script, no writing, no numbers, no speech bubbles, no lamps, no diyas, no candles, no fire, no flames. Exactly two human figures and exactly two birds.
